verdict.rationale: The only first-party sign of approval gating is a Slack docs page titled "charts, tables, and approvals" [openclaw-docs-126], plus a reference to "deterministic policy" in the architecture overview [openclaw-docs-111]. The exec docs describe a mutating shell surface but say nothing about command allowlists, approval prompts, or elevated modes [openclaw-docs-19]. A community commenter describes the default as full, root-like access rather than opt-in [openclaw-comm-10]. missing for 10: documented exec command allowlists, documented approval-prompt flow for dangerous actions, per-action opt-in elevated mode, deny-by-default configuration, hands-on corroboration
